note:
What the fixtures actually look like, sourced rather than inferred from a difficulty rating.

Every `point` is something a named outlet on the verified-100 list published for Gameweek 3. Where a fixture has no recorded points for a club's attack or defence, that means nothing was found — not that there is nothing to say. An empty list is a gap being reported honestly.

WRITTEN 31 AUGUST. The Gameweek 3 deadline is 18:30 BST on Friday 4 September; the first match kicks off ninety minutes later. Friday's press conferences have not happened, so the predicted line-ups recorded here are Fantasy Football Scout's early drafts, which the site revises through the week. The transfer window also does not close until 1 September, which is why the Arsenal v Chelsea notes flag Enzo Fernández rather than assume him.

Deadline conflict worth recording: one page returned a Gameweek 3 deadline of 19:30, while Fantasy Football Scout state 18:30 BST in several places. 18:30 BST is used here; the 19:30 figure is most likely a central-European rendering of the same moment.

fixtures.headline: The first match after the deadline, against a side that conceded five last time out — and a Liverpool back line missing three defenders.

defence.point: Ipswich conceded five goals in their last match, which is the single number the Liverpool case for Gameweek 3 rests on.
Noussair Diop, signed from Fulham after a strong World Cup for Morocco, is expected to start at centre-back.

attack.point: Tzolakis is the most-transferred-in goalkeeper of the gameweek at £4.5m — managers are buying the promoted-side keeper, not backing the promoted-side attack.

defence.point: Conor Bradley (knee), Giovanni Leoni (knee) and Joe Gomez (muscle) are all out. Szoboszlai, a central midfielder, was used at right-back in Gameweek 2 — that is how thin the cover is.
Liverpool have not kept a clean sheet yet this season, and Iraola spent a press conference explaining why they are hard to come by right now.

attack.point: Iraola is short in the forward line — Salah has not been truly replaced, and Ekitike is out with an Achilles injury until around December.
Szoboszlai took every Liverpool set piece in Gameweek 1 and has since scored a penalty. With Salah gone the spot kicks look like his.
The opening run — Ipswich, Sunderland, Fulham — contains three winnable fixtures, so this is the start of a stretch rather than a one-off.

fixtures.headline: Scout call it the best attacking fixture of the round. Newcastle have not beaten Bournemouth in eight league attempts.

defence.point: Lewis Hall (£5.0m) is near the top of the transfers-in column, alongside Wissa and Elanga.
No Gameweek 3 clean-sheet odds have been published by the verified sources yet, so the defensive case here is currently unquantified.

attack.point: Isak has all the underlying numbers wanted from a premium forward and gets arguably the best possible fixture for an attacking asset — on 16.2% ownership and outside the top twenty transfers in.
Wissa scored his first of the season on Saturday having assisted against Liverpool: six shots across two matches, three of them big chances.
Elanga has two goals from four attempts under Matthias Jaissle.
Newcastle have a great run of fixtures to Gameweek 10 and no European football to rotate around.

defence.point: Newcastle have not won any of their last eight league meetings with Bournemouth — the one hard record cutting against an otherwise clean fixture read.

fixtures.headline: Second-highest clean-sheet odds of the gameweek, and a Brentford attack sitting on shots that have not become goals yet.

defence.point: Brentford have the second-highest clean-sheet odds for Gameweek 3.
Kristoffer Ajer (£4.5m) is one of only four defenders in the game to have banked defensive contribution points in both gameweeks.

attack.point: Kevin Schade (£6.0m) already has eight shots inside the box.
Igor Thiago is a notable expected-goals underachiever — the numbers are good, the goals have not arrived.
Thiago is a HOLD: good underlying numbers, good fixture, no reason to chase points elsewhere.

defence.point: Dayann Methalie serves a one-match ban carried over from five yellow cards in France.

attack.point: Mamadou Sangaré (£5.6m) is named for defensive contributions in this fixture and separately as a midfielder Scout prefer to Elanga at similar money.

fixtures.headline: A patched-up Brighton attack against the cheap Leeds midfielders half the community is weighing up.

attack.point: Brighton have Evan Ferguson and Jack Hinshelwood out and Georginio Rutter questionable.
Yankuba Minteh remains out — the absence that pushed De Cuyper into an advanced role in Gameweek 1 has not closed.
No verified source published a Gameweek 3 assessment of De Cuyper himself in this research pass. That is a gap, not a verdict.
Anton Stach (£6.0m) is named by Scout among the midfielders they would rather own than Elanga at comparable money.

fixtures.headline: Two sides missing their most important attacking name apiece.

defence.point: Sepp van den Berg (groin) and Antoni Milambo (knee) remain out, and new signing El Hadji Malick Diouf may not be registered in time.

attack.point: Jean-Philippe Mateta is ruled out — a muscular injury sustained in training, with at least four weeks expected.
Palace are one of only two clubs sitting below Coventry for both goal difference and points.

fixtures.headline: The fixture the whole gameweek is built around. Scout's picks piece is titled 'Piling up on Man City'.

attack.point: Haaland surely dominates the armband discussion for a home fixture against Coventry — the open question is whether to activate the Triple Captain.
Cherki has four attacking returns in two matches and is creating a chance every sixteen minutes. BUY.
Foden topped the whole game's xGI table in Gameweek 2 with two assists, having missed two big chances of his own.
Foden (£7.0m) and Cherki (£7.6m) are the cheaper City options being weighed to complete a triple-up alongside Haaland.
Semenyo crossed for Haaland's opener, created three chances and had two efforts from narrow angles.
City have won both games under Maresca.

defence.point: Only Palace and Spurs are below Coventry for goal difference and points tally — exactly the kind of fixture where you want exposure to a Man City attacker.

fixtures.headline: Gibbs-White at the City Ground against a Spurs side that was still signing forwards three days earlier.

attack.point: Penalty-taking Morgan Gibbs-White (£7.9m) hauled at Anfield, continuing the form that brought seven goals in his final seven starts last season.
Omar Marmoush joined on loan from Manchester City with a £60m obligation to buy, and De Zerbi has indicated he sees him as a central striker.
Savinho arrived for £85m in the same window; Spurs were pursuing three new forwards.
Marmoush had the best shots-per-90 rate among Fantasy midfielders last season at 3.49 — among forwards only Haaland bettered it.
Spurs sit alongside Palace as one of the two clubs below Coventry on both goal difference and points.

fixtures.headline: Villa without their new midfielder for three more gameweeks, against the promoted side who beat Bruno Fernandes's Manchester United in Gameweek 1.

attack.point: Hull held Manchester United to a Bruno Fernandes blank in Gameweek 1 — 144,000 managers sold him on the back of it and regretted it a week later.

defence.point: Villa were much better defensively on Monday night and may have turned a corner.

attack.point: João Gomes sits out the next three gameweeks, serving a ban after a violent conduct red card on his debut.
Ollie Watkins was the most-sold forward of Gameweek 2 at 182,000 transfers out, on a reported move to Al-Hilal.

fixtures.headline: A trickier away trip on the ticker, against the defence that has given up the second-most big chances in the league.

defence.point: Everton have conceded a league-second-worst ten big chances in the first two gameweeks.

attack.point: Bruno Fernandes has to be considered after Sunday's epic haul, although he has a trickier fixture away at Everton.
Mbeumo is on many chopping blocks; the published verdict is KEEP rather than sell.
Amad will not be involved — he is out for a little longer, hoping to return before the international break.
Matthijs de Ligt and Mason Mount have been working hard to come back from injury.

fixtures.headline: The best defence in the league against an attack that has scored seven in two — and a Chelsea team sheet with four names missing.

defence.point: Arsenal have kept clean sheets in both the Community Shield and Gameweek 1, and the underlying clean-sheet projections are extremely strong.
Arsenal continue to ride high in the clean sheet odds.
Raya (£6.0m), Calafiori (£5.6m) or Konsa (£4.4m) are worth contemplating even though Chelsea have netted seven times.
Predicted 4-3-3: Raya; Timber, Saliba, Gabriel, Hincapié; Rice, Zubimendi, Ødegaard; Saka, Gyökeres, Trossard.

attack.point: Gyökeres is in excellent form, having netted eight goals in his last twelve matches.
Saka (£9.5m) could make a late charge for the Picks.
Gyökeres to strike again in a comfortable Arsenal win.

defence.point: Chelsea are without Marc Cucurella, Jamie Gittens and Estêvão, all with hamstring injuries, and Wesley Fofana is suspended after his red card.
Predicted 4-2-3-1: Sánchez; James, Adarabioyo, Chalobah, Gusto; Santos, Caicedo; Palmer, Fernández, Neto; João Pedro.

attack.point: João Pedro has bagged a goal and an assist in both matches and is hard to bench at such high ownership.
Chelsea have netted seven times in two matches — this is the strongest attack Arsenal have faced.
Enzo Fernández appears in the predicted XI, but the transfer window closes on 1 September and Manchester City's interest is unresolved.
